study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Yang S et al., Cerebral Cortex, 2025
study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative modeling of brain morphometry in self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To quantify individual deviations from the normative range of brain morphometric variation in children with Self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (SeLECTS) and to assess their associations with clinical manifestations and cognitive functions.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper explicitly states that the normative model was trained on data from the developing Chinese Color Nest Project (devCCNP).
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: The data for model training consists of two samples: the CKG sample and the PEK sample. Samples from the two different centers are both sourced from the developing Chinese Color Nest Project (devCCNP).

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: Structural MRI processing pipelines were primarily built using FreeSurfer (Fischl et al. 2001) and FSL (Smith et al. 2004). T1-weight data processing included cortical segmentation and surface reconstruction analyses. Anatomical surfaces were generated from the individual T1w image in native space using the recon-all command in FreeSurfer.

nm1_model_origin.supporting_text: To ensure generalizability and robustness, we followed the normative modeling framework provided by CentileBrain (Ge et al. 2024). clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group comparisons of deviation percentages were done with 2-proportion z-test. Associations between the number of regions with deviations and clinical/cognitive variables were tested with Spearman correlation. Associations between averaged deviations and clinical variables were tested with Pearson's correlation. All tests used a significance threshold of P < 0.05 with FDR correction.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Children with SeLECTS showed a higher proportion of regions with infra-normal subcortical volume deviations compared to controls, and the number of regions with deviations correlated with disease duration, seizure frequency, and cognition.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The study found that while the overall distribution of brain morphometric deviations in children with SeLECTS was similar to healthy controls, a higher proportion of SeLECTS patients had infra-normal deviations in subcortical volume across any number of regions (χ2=7.54, P=0.04). No significant group differences were found for individual brain regions. Within the SeLECTS group, the number of regions with supra-normal subcortical volume deviations correlated with disease duration (R2=0.06, P=0.05) and seizure frequency (R2=0.11, P=0.01), while the number of regions with infra-normal cortical thickness deviations correlated with Raven's total score (R2=0.07, P=0.05).

caa10_key_limitations.answer: The study limitations include the need for a larger sample for more stable models, the cross-sectional design which doesn't capture longitudinal changes, and the limited set of covariates (only age and sex) which omits other demographic, developmental, and lifestyle factors.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: There are several limitations pertinent to this study. First, our study could benefit from the inclusion of a larger sample of children, which would result in more stable and generalizable normative models. Secondly, the morphometric measures were based on cross-sectional and did not capture longitudinal changes. ... Thirdly, the model only considers sex and age, and demographic, developmental, and lifestyle factors were not included in the analysis.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study compared the predictive performance of normative deviation z-scores versus observed morphometric measures for diagnostic classification (SeLECTS vs. control) using a support vector classification (SVC) model, finding that neither performed well, with AUCs of 0.56 and 0.48, respectively.
